name: TAJIKISTAN

flag.title: Tajikistan
flag.note: Tricolour: red, white, green + crown & stars

lead: Tajikistan is a country of mountains. About 90% of it is peaks and valleys. The Pamirs are called the Roof of the World. Half the country sits above 3,000 m.
geo: Ismoil Somoni Peak, at 7,495 m, is the tallest summit in the former Soviet Union. The Fedchenko Glacier is 77 km long. It is the longest outside the polar regions.
Over 900 rivers cut through the highlands. The Nurek Dam is 300 m tall, one of the world's highest. Its 70 km lake fills a canyon and glows bright blue.
animals: The snow leopard is a ghostly grey spotted cat. About 250–280 live in the high Pamirs, hunting ibex and wild sheep. Locals call it the ghost of the mountains.
The Marco Polo sheep is the national animal. Its curly horns grow over 1.5 m long, the longest of any wild sheep. It grazes above 4,000 m.
culture: Tajiks never turn a guest away. Tea, flatbread (non), and dried fruit cover the dastarkhan, a spread-cloth. Osh, the national dish, is rice with lamb and carrots.
On 21 March, Tajiks celebrate Navruz, the Persian New Year. Cooks stir a sweet porridge, sumalak, all night. People wear bright atlas silk dresses and embroidered skullcaps called tubeteika.
history: Sogdian merchants carried silk and gold along these passes for a thousand years. The Samanid Empire (9th–10th centuries) made nearby Bukhara a centre of Persian poetry and science.
Russia took the region in the 1800s. Tajikistan became a Soviet republic in 1929. It became independent on 9 September 1991. A civil war ended in 1997.
wows: Dushanbe means 'Monday' in Tajik, after a Monday market.
In 2011, Dushanbe's 165 m flagpole was briefly the world's tallest.
The 77 km Fedchenko Glacier is the longest outside the polar regions.
Lake Iskanderkul is named after Alexander the Great, who legend says drowned his horse there.
A 12-metre sleeping Buddha was found buried in northern Tajikistan in 1966.
The Nurek Dam is 300 m tall, one of the highest ever built.

myths.fact: Travellers have driven the Pamir Highway for decades. The hard part is distance, not getting in.
Valley summers reach 30 °C. Dushanbe is warm from May to October.
